title: A busy day in the cab
hook: Two stated cases: explore an income-target stopping rule.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How an income-target stopping rule affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines Hours, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare an income-target stopping rule in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: A toy worker stops exactly at income 200 and earns 20 per hour. After how many hours do they stop?

provenance.sourceEntryOriginal: - **7.** New York cab drivers quit earlier on high-earning days, consistent with daily income targets (Camerer, Babcock, Loewenstein & Thaler, 1997). **\[contested\]** Farber (2005, 2015) found weaker evidence.
